claims: Artemis II is NASA's first crewed mission of the Artemis program.
Artemis II is scheduled to launch no earlier than April 1, 2026 from Kennedy Space Center, FL.
Artemis II will conduct a ~10-day lunar flyby.
Artemis II will fly four astronauts around the Moon and back.
Artemis II will test the Orion spacecraft's life-support systems.
Artemis II marks the first human trip to the vicinity of the Moon in over 50 years.
The crew of Artemis II consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
The duration of Artemis II is approximately 10 days.
The goal of Artemis II is to test critical Orion spacecraft systems, including life support and manual piloting.
Artemis II is to prepare for future Artemis lunar landings beginning with Artemis III.
The path of Artemis II is a free-return trajectory.
The Artemis II trajectory will take the crew around the far side of the Moon.
The maximum distance of Artemis II beyond the far side of the Moon is 4,700 miles.
Artemis II features the first woman (Christina Koch) to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
Artemis II features the first person of color (Victor Glover) to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
Artemis II features the first Canadian (Jeremy Hansen) to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
Artemis II is a flyby mission.
Artemis II is not a landing mission.
Artemis II aims to set a record for the farthest distance from Earth traveled by humans.
Artemis II aims to exceed the Apollo 13 path.
Artemis II will test the Orion spacecraft's heat shield at 25,000 mph upon re-entering Earth's atmosphere.
Artemis II follows the successful uncrewed Artemis I flight in 2022.
